anatomy.flutter: ActiveIndicator is one StatefulWidget: a Stack with an AnimatedPositioned+AnimatedOpacity+AnimatedBuilder pill first, then a Padding>Row of KeyedSubtree children, all measured via a GlobalKey-per-item _measure() scheduled post-frame.
anatomy.web: Split into a hook (useActiveIndicator, returning containerRef/indicatorRef/arrivalRef and running its own MutationObserver+ResizeObserver effect) and a presentational component (ActiveIndicator, a <span> pill nested inside another <span> for the arrival animation), composed manually onto a host by each caller (Tabs, ToggleGroup, SidebarMenu).
anatomy.note: The web's hook/component split exists so the pill can watch an arbitrary Radix primitive's DOM mutations (data-state) without threading controlled state through it; Flutter has no DOM to observe and instead takes an explicit activeIndex prop, folding the two web pieces into one widget. This is the correct per-platform shape for the same measured-pill mechanism, not a missing piece.

api.flutter: ActiveIndicator({activeIndex, indicator, children, padding=EdgeInsets.zero, gap=0, moveDuration, jellyAlignment=Alignment.center}) — activeIndex is an explicit int (out-of-range/-1 hides the pill), moveDuration overrides the 250ms default (Duration.zero for the theme-toggle snap case), jellyAlignment matches Tabs' line variant pivot.
api.web: useActiveIndicator<T>(activeSelector='[data-state="on"],[data-state="active"]', arrivalAnimation='anim-change', attributeName='data-state') returns refs; ActiveIndicator({indicatorRef, arrivalRef, className, children}) renders the pill span, with selection driven implicitly by which DOM node currently matches activeSelector.
api.note: Flutter's index-driven API and the web's selector/attribute-driven API are the same feature expressed the right way for each runtime: Dart has a typed widget tree to index into, the DOM needs a CSS selector and a MutationObserver. The Sidebar's custom '[data-active="true"]' / 'data-active' parameters (documented in the Variants section) have no separate Flutter counterpart because Flutter's version never needed the workaround the DOM did (colliding with Radix's own data-state on a wrapping CollapsibleTrigger).

states.flutter: _ActiveIndicatorState models exactly three visual states via _placed/_held/_target: not-yet-placed (opacity/travel suppressed with Duration.zero), placed-and-active (travels + squashes via AnimatedPositioned/_jelly), and deselected (rect held at _held, only opacity animates, jelly guarded off in _replayJelly's null-target early return).
states.web: Docs States section enumerates the same three ('on first mount' — no travel; 'after selection changes' — travels then squashes; 'nothing active' — opacity 0, ToggleGroup only) and explicitly marks hover/pressed/disabled/loading/success/error N/A because 'it is a visual echo of whatever option is selected, never a target of its own.'

disabled.flutter: No disabled parameter or branch exists anywhere in active_indicator.dart — IgnorePointer already removes it from hit-testing unconditionally, regardless of any option's own disabled state.
disabled.web: Docs States section: 'disabled... are all N/A: the pill carries pointer-events-none and aria-hidden — it is a visual echo... Those states belong to the option underneath it.'
disabled.note: Both sides agree the pill itself has no disabled concept; disabled styling belongs to the host option (Tab/ToggleGroupItem/SidebarMenuButton), documented on those components' own pages, not here.

interaction.flutter: _measure() is scheduled via WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback on every build and only calls setState when a rect actually changed, covering a selection change, a resize, a font swap or a child appearing — the doc comment states this 'covers everything the web's MutationObserver + ResizeObserver pair covers.'
interaction.web: The effect installs a MutationObserver (subtree:true, attributeFilter:[attributeName]) for selection changes and a ResizeObserver on the container for size changes, both disconnected on cleanup, per the Responsive section's 'Re-measures on: attribute mutation' / 'Re-measures on: resize' rows.

semantics.flutter: No Semantics/ExcludeSemantics wrapper appears anywhere in active_indicator.dart — only IgnorePointer (hit-testing) is applied around the AnimatedOpacity/pill subtree, so nothing explicitly removes the pill from the platform accessibility tree.
semantics.web: The outer <span ref={indicatorRef} aria-hidden ...> in components/ui/active-indicator.tsx line 174 always carries aria-hidden, and the docs Accessibility section states 'Always set on the outer indicator span... the pill is a sighted-user affordance layered on top of that, not a second source of truth.'
semantics.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The Flutter port relies on IgnorePointer alone, which only affects touch/pointer hit-testing, not the semantics tree a screen reader walks; unlike the web's explicit aria-hidden, a TalkBack/VoiceOver user could still land focus-order narration on the decorative pill widget (e.g. if `indicator` ever contains any semantic content), where the web guarantees it is excluded. This is a real, if narrow, gap — add Semantics(excludeSemantics: true) or ExcludeSemantics around the pill subtree to close it.
